project.name: virtuoso-cli
project.description: CLI tool to control Cadence Virtuoso from the command line — three binaries (vcli main CLI, vtui TUI, virtuoso-daemon background bridge relay). Provides session/job management, Maestro flow control, Spectre netlist/PSF parsing, Ocean expression evaluation, SSH-tunneled remote EDA workflows, and a SKILL-over-TCP bridge to a running Virtuoso instance. The companion skill catalog under .claude/skills automates analog IC design workflows (schematic capture, simulation sweeps, optimization, g_m/I_d characterization).

nodes.summary: VirtuosoClient TCP bridge to the Cadence Virtuoso daemon. Wraps the raw STX/NAK TCP protocol, drives SKILL execution with capability gating and an evalstring whitelist, exposes layout/schematic/maestro/window operation handles, and manages transactions and SSH tunneling.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the STX/ETX framed protocol; many methods assemble SKILL strings via the *_ops builders; capability + whitelist enforced on raw skill exec; transactions are stored in std::cell::RefCell (single-threaded client).

nodes.name: src/client/editor.rs
nodes.summary: Layout and Schematic editor builder structs (LayoutEditor, SchematicEditor) that collect SKILL commands into a batch and execute them as a single call.
nodes.languageNotes: Two zero-copy builders over VirtuosoClient; all unit structs use LayoutOps/SchematicOps for SKILL string generation.

nodes.name: src/client/layout_ops.rs
nodes.summary: LayoutOps SKILL string builder: rodCreateRect, rodCreatePolygon, rodCreatePath, rodCreateVia, rodCreateInstance, xstOutDoTranslate. XstreamOutRequest config struct for tape-out streaming.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure SKILL-string formatters backed by escape_skill_string; XstreamOutRequest is a borrowed &str struct; most ops are unit structs.

nodes.name: src/client/library_ops.rs
nodes.summary: LibraryOps read-only SKILL builder for ddGetLibList(). Tiny unit struct used by the library list command.
nodes.languageNotes: Single method returning a SKILL lambda string; used by commands/library.rs.

nodes.name: src/client/maestro_ops.rs
nodes.summary: MaestroOps builder for SKILL strings driving Cadence Maestro simulation setup (sessions, maeGetSetup, maeSetAnalysis, sweeps, ocean export). ExportWaveformRequest DTO for waveform export.
nodes.languageNotes: Long SKILL strings with embedded version-dependent branches (IC23 vs IC25); ExportWaveformRequest wraps file paths.

nodes.name: src/client/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module index for the client submodule, exporting bridge, editor, layout_ops, library_ops, maestro_ops, schematic_ops, skill_loading (private), skill_runtime (pub(crate)), skill_sexp, symbol_ops, whitelist, window_ops.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure re-exports; no code.

nodes.name: src/client/schematic_ops.rs
nodes.summary: SchematicOps SKILL builders for instance creation, wire/instance deletion, property edits, and cellview save/commit. Prepends a cv_guard() that errors when no cellview is open.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses geGetEditCellView() rather than RB_SCH_CV for cv binding; cv_guard() forces explicit cellview open.

nodes.name: src/client/skill_runtime.rs
nodes.summary: Internal helpers for SKILL/JSON interop: escape_string, string_literal, require_identifier, require_transport, require_non_nil, decode_json, decode_json_payload.
nodes.languageNotes: pub(crate) helpers shared across commands/*; centralizes error mapping from VirtuosoResult to VirtuosoError.

nodes.name: src/client/skill_sexp.rs
nodes.summary: S-expression parser for SKILL output. SexpVal enum (Nil/Bool/Str/Atom/List) plus parse_sexp and sexp_to_str_list helpers used to convert daemon responses.
nodes.languageNotes: Recursive-descent parser over a byte slice with peek/consume primitives.

nodes.name: src/client/symbol_ops.rs
nodes.summary: SymbolOps builders for symbol inspection and schSchemToPinList → schPinListToSymbol generation with safe no-overwrite and temp-symbol cleanup.
nodes.languageNotes: Generates long unwieldy SKILL strings with errset/unwindProtect; uses uuid for temp symbol names.

nodes.name: src/client/whitelist.rs
nodes.summary: evalstring whitelist: blocks dangerous SKILL patterns (system(, sh(, curl, rm -rf, evalstring, etc.) at the CLI before serialization. EvalstringWhitelist supports a sandbox mode that disables evalstring outright.
nodes.languageNotes: Substring + substring-with-allowlist (hiFlush/hiShell) + word-boundary regex matching; case-insensitive.

nodes.name: src/client/window_ops.rs
nodes.summary: WindowOps for window listing and the safe bootstrap interface. BootstrapTarget + BootstrapAction::LoadFile load SKILL programs from a canonicalized scratch dir; raw SKILL execution is forbidden through this path.
nodes.languageNotes: Targets windows by explicit X11-style id; defends against accidental targeting via required expected_name_pattern; path canonicalization enforces scratch-root containment.

nodes.name: src/commands/cell.rs
nodes.summary: CLI command handlers for cell-level operations: open (with mode + dry_run), save, close. Delegates to VirtuosoClient::open_cell_view / save_current_cellview / close_current_cellview.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure JSON-output wrappers; takes CommandContext to share config.

nodes.name: src/commands/library.rs
nodes.summary: CLI command handler for library list; parses ddGetLibList s-expression output via skill_sexp.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses execute_skill_unchecked — capability already enforced at RPC dispatch; calls sexp_to_str_list for output.

nodes.name: src/commands/maestro.rs
nodes.summary: CLI command handlers for Maestro session control: open/close/list_sessions, set_var, run_analysis, sweep, ocean, and staging guard for ADE windows. StagingGuard ensures window stability before simulation.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest module in the batch; mostly JSON-output wrappers calling VirtuosoClient::maestro with shell_quote for path escaping.

nodes.name: src/commands/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module index for CLI command submodules: cell, config, design, diag, init, library, maestro, process, schema, schematic, session, sim, skill, symbol, transaction, transport_daemon (native-ssh only), tunnel, window.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure re-exports; transport_daemon gated on `native-ssh` feature.

nodes.name: src/commands/process.rs
nodes.summary: Process corner / DC / AC characterization command handlers (char). Runs Spectre sweeps through the daemon and accumulates data points. OpVals is a small JSON values struct.
nodes.languageNotes: Drives simulator + design commands directly via execute_skill with string_literal escaping.

nodes.name: src/commands/schema.rs
nodes.summary: Static CLI schema dump for the `vcli schema` introspection command. Hardcodes the full command/flag structure as a serde_json Value.
nodes.languageNotes: No I/O; just a static json!() tree keyed by command name.

nodes.name: src/commands/schematic.rs
nodes.summary: CLI command handlers for schematic editing: open/place/wire/delete/property/save. Defines the Orient (R0/R90/.../MYR90) value enum and a YAML-style SchematicSpec parser.
nodes.languageNotes: Spec types (SchematicSpec/SpecTarget/SpecInstance/SpecConnection/SpecGlobal/SpecPin) support declarative schematic editing via YAML.

nodes.name: src/commands/symbol.rs
nodes.summary: CLI command handlers for symbol inspection (from SKILL s-expression JSON) and generation (delegates to SymbolOps::generate).
nodes.languageNotes: Tag-based JSON response (success/notFound/failed); uses parse_sexp for response decoding.

nodes.name: src/commands/transaction.rs
nodes.summary: CLI command handlers for Virtuoso transactions: begin, commit, rollback, diff, status. Thin wrappers around VirtuosoClient::tx_* methods.
nodes.languageNotes: All take &CommandContext; tx_diff/tx_status return Option to signal no active transaction.

nodes.name: src/version.rs
nodes.summary: VirtuosoVersion enum (IC23/IC25/Unknown) and detect_version() that probes the daemon via getVersion(t) and parse_ic_version().
nodes.languageNotes: detect_version uses execute_skill_idempotent_probe so it survives a stale queued ticket.

nodes.name: sim.rs

nodes.name: tunnel.rs

nodes.name: window.rs

nodes.name: profile.rs
nodes.summary: Profile (Virtuoso environment) resolution and binding across venv, user, and local scopes. Resolves profile from explicit flag / env var / venv / user config, and binds/clears it for child processes. Defines ProfileResolution, BindScope.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust module with serde-free data structures, env::var probing, and Drop-side cleanup of env vars for spawned processes.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for the typed RPC layer. Declares `dispatcher` and `schema` submodules; replaces raw SKILL strings with `{method, params}` calls that map to SKILL expressions and return typed JSON.
nodes.languageNotes: Trivial module-facade file (13 lines); purely submodule declarations plus documentation.

nodes.name: schema.rs
nodes.summary: RPC schema definitions: Method/Param/RpcSchema structs plus standard_schema() returning all built-in RPC methods (schematic, library, design, simulation, etc.) with JSON-Schema-like metadata. Drives discoverable, type-safe API for AI agents.
nodes.languageNotes: Large file (1216 lines) dominated by a single static-literal schema constructor; serde-derived Serialize/Deserialize types.

nodes.name: runtime_paths.rs
nodes.summary: Centralized filesystem path resolution for the bridge runtime. Honours VB_CACHE_DIR / VB_LOG_DIR / VB_HOME / XDG_CACHE_HOME env vars, falls back to dirs::cache_dir(), and provides a legacy_cache_file API for pre-refactor state files.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-Path module adapted from virtuoso-bridge-lite (Python). Uses std::env::var_os and PathBuf exclusively; no I/O.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: SKILL Finder client — query Cadence SKILL API docs from .fnd databases. Supports Fuzzy/Prefix/Suffix/Exact/Regex search modes, remote-host cache (~/.cache/virtuoso_bridge/skill_finder/<host>/), lazy sync, and refresh.
nodes.languageNotes: Module gated `#![allow(dead_code)]`; exports SearchMode enum, SKILLFinder struct, search/sync helpers, and re-exports parser types.

nodes.name: parser.rs
nodes.summary: Hand-rolled state-machine parser for Cadence .fnd SKILL Finder database files. Yields SkillEntry triples (name, syntax, description) tolerant of comments and trailing fields.
nodes.languageNotes: Recursive-descent-style lexer without regex; comment-aware, treats SKILL string literals across newlines.

nodes.name: maestro_csv.rs
nodes.summary: Parser for Cadence Maestro "Detail" CSV exports (maeExportOutputView). Produces MaestroResult/Point/Output structs with sweep parameters and per-point measurement data, including optional raw_csv passthrough.
nodes.languageNotes: Serde-derived data model; CSV parsing helpers with HashMap-backed design variables and outputs.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for Spectre-related types. Aggregates jobs, maestro_csv, parsers, runner submodules.
nodes.languageNotes: Tiny (4-line) submodule facade.

nodes.name: job_progress.rs
nodes.summary: JobProgressTracker — polls a Spectre spectre.out log, parses progress lines (iteration count, time point), and emits JobEvent::Progress via a JobEventSink. Backs the streaming progress UI.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses std::fs, atomic byte-position tracking, periodic size checks; throttled reads via Instant elapsed check.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Streaming event primitives. Defines JobEvent (Started/Progress/Completed/Failed/Cancelled tagged enum), JobEventSink trait, StdoutSink/ChannelSink impls, and helpers for fan-out / throttling.
nodes.languageNotes: Tagged enum with serde rename_all="snake_case"; Arc<dyn JobEventSink> fan-out; tokio mpsc integration.

nodes.name: linux_rename.rs
nodes.summary: Cross-glibc wrapper for renameat2(..., RENAME_NOREPLACE). Tries dlsym, then raw SYS_renameat2 syscall, then a non-atomic lstat + renameat fallback for CentOS 7 / glibc 2.17.
nodes.languageNotes: cfg(target_os="linux")-gated FFI with libc::c_int / c_uint, raw pointers, and unsafe extern "C" function-pointer typedef.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for platform compatibility shims. Currently exposes linux_rename on Linux only.
nodes.languageNotes: Trivial (8 lines); only includes linux_rename under cfg(target_os = "linux").

nodes.name: test_env.rs
nodes.summary: Sentinel module documenting that env-mutating tests must use #[serial] from serial_test. Empty body, exists only to give future env-aware test helpers an obvious home.
nodes.languageNotes: #![cfg(test)] only; no runtime code.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Top-level in-module test suite for vcli. Configures Config / SSHRunner / SessionInfo, runs SSH command-construction tests, env-var validation, and JSON round-trips. No network or Virtuoso required.
nodes.languageNotes: Large (2376 lines) file containing many #[cfg(test)] mod submodules; uses serial_test::serial for env-touching tests.

nodes.name: diff.rs
nodes.summary: SchematicDiff: structured diff between two SchematicSnapshots. Tracks instances added/removed/modified, nets added/removed, and pins added/removed with per-parameter old/new values.
nodes.languageNotes: Serde-derived structs; computes diffs by HashMap lookup on instance/pin names.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Transaction system facade: Transaction / TransactionManager lifecycle over a single VirtuosoClient. Tracks the active tx plus committed history and supports begin/commit/rollback semantics.
nodes.languageNotes: RefCell-backed interior mutability so tx_* methods take &self; HashMap of net assignments per tx.

nodes.name: snapshot.rs
nodes.summary: SchematicSnapshot: point-in-time capture of a cellview (lib/cell/view + instances, nets, pins, terminal connectivity). Round-trips through serde for diffing and persistence.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure data types plus a capture async fn that talks to VirtuosoClient; uses HashMap for instance/pin lookups.

nodes.name: vtui.rs
nodes.summary: vtui binary entrypoint. Declares all library modules and re-exports the public surface (Capability/Set, standard_schema, SchematicDiff/Snapshot, TransactionManager); calls tui::run_tui() from main.
nodes.languageNotes: 44-line mod aggregator with `#![allow(dead_code)]`; thin main() that delegates to tui::run_tui.

nodes.name: gui_runner.py
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for the virtuoso-gui-debug skill. Parses arguments, validates scenarios, dispatches FakeExecutor / LiveExecutor / LocalExecutor, and emits exactly one compact JSON object per invocation (with structured exit codes 0/1/2).
nodes.languageNotes: Python 3 script using pathlib-based sys.path manipulation to load the sibling vgui_runner package; strict exit-code contract and single-line JSON stdout pattern.

nodes.name: command_runner.py
nodes.summary: Fixed-argv subprocess transport for the live executor. Defines CommandError, CommandResult, CommandRunner base class, plus LocalRunner (subprocess.run with cleaned env) and SshRunner (safe shlex.quote of a fixed vcli argv). Rejects shell strings, NUL, newlines, and any remote argv injection.
nodes.languageNotes: Python with frozen dataclass for CommandResult; enforces a strict environment allowlist (PATH, LANG, LC_ALL, HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME, VB_PORT, VB_REMOTE_HOST) plus VCLI_CAPABILITY=admin.

nodes.name: engine.py
nodes.summary: State machine and step runner for scenario execution. Defines RunState / StepPhase / StepOutcome enums, the Executor ABC, FakeExecutor (deterministic offline outcomes keyed by step/phase/attempt), and the Runner that drives precheck → baseline → execute → verify → recover with retries and JSONL tracing.
nodes.languageNotes: Python ABC protocol with Runner class owning retry/rollback semantics; uses frozen tuples for step outputs and dataclass RunSummary for results.

nodes.name: live_executor.py
nodes.summary: Real vcli/SSH/X11 executor implementing the Executor protocol against an injected command runner. Binds session/PID/DISPLAY/window at precheck, holds a per-DISPLAY flock, dispatches GUI actions via fixed `vcli window action-x11` argv, sanitizes typed input out of errors, and supports a fast --direct path plus action-x11-batch.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest module in the package (~1026 lines); uses fcntl.flock, MappingProxyType, regex-based argv templating, and a dedicated _DisplayLock context manager.

nodes.name: local_executor.py
nodes.summary: Direct xdotool executor for scenarios whose DISPLAY is local to the runner. Implements the Executor protocol via xdotool (search/getwindowgeometry/click/type/key) and ImageMagick import for screenshots. Supports SCROLL (xdotool buttons 4/5/6/7) and binds target window by PID at precheck.
nodes.languageNotes: Python class with private helpers (_xdotool, _window_geometry, _absolute_coords) translating relative coords to absolute via xdotool geometry output.

nodes.name: model.py
nodes.summary: Strict scenario parser producing deeply immutable dataclasses (Scenario, Step, CellView) with the Operation enum, per-operation argument schemas, integer/string/predicate allowlists, and ScenarioValidationError on any deviation. Supports version 1.0 round-trip via MappingProxyType.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses MappingProxyType / tuple / frozenset for deep immutability; central OP_ARG_SCHEMAS, INT_ARG_KEYS, STR_ARG_KEYS, BUTTON_ARG_KEYS, WINDOW_WAIT_ALLOWED_STATES, SCROLL_ALLOWED_DIRECTIONS tables.

nodes.name: trace.py
nodes.summary: Append-only JSONL event log with immediate flush. Provides Event dataclass and Trace class emitting monotonic sequence-numbered, UTC-timestamped state/step/attempt/outcome/duration/details records.
nodes.languageNotes: Tiny module: Event dataclass + Trace class with lazy file open and explicit close().

nodes.name: test_command_runner.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for command_runner covering the 2026-09-01 live-executor security contract: local subprocess uses shell=False, environment is cleaned to the allowlist, VCLI_CAPABILITY=admin is set, timeouts yield structured CommandResult, SSH mode accepts only safe hosts and a fixed vcli argv, and NUL/newline/extra-remote-command argv is rejected.
nodes.languageNotes: unittest-based; uses a RecordingRunner fake rather than mocking subprocess directly; macOS-tolerant (filters __CF_* and LC_CTYPE leaked env vars).

nodes.name: test_engine.py
nodes.summary: Tests for engine state machine and FakeExecutor: per-phase success/failure, attempt-based retries, recover/rollback paths, atomic task.json output, and trace event sequence. Validates happy-path, precheck/baseline failures, recover-then-retry, no-retry-when-max_retries=0, and final FAILED event payload.
nodes.languageNotes: unittest; uses tempfile.mkdtemp for per-test output dirs and an outcomes_to_dict helper to build FakeExecutor scenarios.

nodes.name: test_live_executor.py
nodes.summary: Largest test module: covers LiveExecutor precheck (session/port/PID/DISPLAY/window/lock), baseline screenshot sanitization, every DSL operation mapping to a fixed vcli argv, verify predicates (database-first), recover rollbacks, typed-input sanitization, _DisplayLock lifecycle, and argv-level session awareness.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a scripted FakeRunner (per-test list of CommandResult/Exception/callable) so no ssh/vcli/X11 is ever invoked; sessions_json and WINDOWS_ONE constants build realistic vcli responses.

nodes.name: test_local_executor.py
nodes.summary: Tests for LocalExecutor (xdotool path) with subprocess.run mocked: precheck (xdotool missing, DISPLAY unreachable, no-window-for-pid, window found, explicit --window-id), execute for every supported operation incl. SCROLL, verify predicates, recover rollback, baseline screenshot, and geometry-guard against missing X server.
nodes.languageNotes: unittest.mock with @mock.patch on shutil.which and _run; constructs mock.Mock completed-process objects to avoid any real subprocess execution.

nodes.name: test_model.py
nodes.summary: Strict scenario-parsing tests for model.py: version 1.0, Operation enum, CellView, root type checks, duplicate step IDs, missing/invalid verifiers, session_id / PID / display rules, timeout/retry bounds, per-operation argument-type validation (40+ operations), verifier predicates, rollback shape, deep immutability, and JSON round-trip.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest single test file in the skill (~875 lines, 29 TestCase classes); uses VALID_SCENARIO dict constant and Scenario.from_dict everywhere; covers negative paths exhaustively.

nodes.name: parse_fake_outcomes
nodes.summary: Reads a fake-outcomes JSON file (list of {step_id, phase, attempt, outcome} dicts), validates each field, and returns {(step_id, phase, attempt): StepOutcome} for FakeExecutor.
nodes.languageNotes: Strict phase allowlist (precheck/baseline/execute/verify/recover) and outcome allowlist (SUCCESS/FAILURE); raises ValueError on first violation.

nodes.name: cmd_validate
nodes.summary: Loads a scenario via Scenario.load and emits either a valid-summary JSON or a structured invalid/error JSON. Returns exit 0 on success, 2 on validation or unexpected error.
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps Scenario.load with two distinct except branches: ScenarioValidationError vs generic Exception.

nodes.name: build_executor
nodes.summary: Factory that returns a (executor, error) tuple for the --executor choice: fake (with optional outcomes file), live (needs session_id + vcli_path + ssh_host), local (needs display + pid). Errors are returned as dicts, not raised, so the CLI can JSON-emit them.
nodes.languageNotes: Lazy imports inside the function for LiveExecutor / LocalExecutor to keep the offline fake path import-light.

nodes.name: cmd_run
nodes.summary: Top-level run handler: builds the executor, loads the scenario, runs Runner.run, emits the final RunSummary JSON, and returns 0/1/2 based on passed/failed/error.
nodes.languageNotes: Reuses build_executor for the (executor, error) tuple and traps broad exceptions to emit a structured error payload.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: argparse entry point: dispatches `validate` and `run` subcommands, builds the executor, ensures output_dir exists, and propagates the exit code.
nodes.languageNotes: Two subcommands (validate, run); never prints human text — all diagnostics go to stderr only.

nodes.name: CommandRunner
nodes.summary: Abstract base for LocalRunner / SshRunner: validates argv (no shell strings, no NUL/newline), then delegates to subclass _run_validated with a timeout.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure template-method: public run() does validation, abstract _run_validated does the actual execution.

nodes.name: LocalRunner
nodes.summary: Runs the fixed argv locally via subprocess.run with shell=False, cleaned environment, universal_newlines, and a hard timeout that surfaces as CommandResult(timed_out=True).
nodes.languageNotes: Tracks duration_ms via time.monotonic; on TimeoutExpired returns (None, '', str(exc), duration_ms, True).

nodes.name: SshRunner
nodes.summary: Runs vcli over SSH using a fixed remote argv constructed by shell-quoting each element with shlex.quote. Validates ssh_host against a strict regex, rejects extra remote commands, returns CommandResult with timed_out/exit_code/duration_ms.
nodes.languageNotes: Performs a structured ConnectError catch (ssh exit 255) separate from generic subprocess errors; refuses any argv whose first element is not the configured vcli_path.

nodes.name: Executor
nodes.summary: Abstract Executor protocol: precheck, baseline, execute, verify, recover — each returns Optional[Dict[str, Any]] where None means OK.
nodes.languageNotes: Five @abstractmethod decorators; no concrete behavior.

nodes.name: FakeExecutor
nodes.summary: Deterministic offline executor: looks up outcomes by (step_id, phase, attempt) and returns {'error': '...'} when the entry is FAILURE, None otherwise. Default outcome is SUCCESS.
nodes.languageNotes: Used by tests and by `gui_runner --executor fake`; no I/O whatsoever.

nodes.name: Runner
nodes.summary: Drives a Scenario through PRECHECK → BASELINE per-step EXECUTE/VERIFY with retries → RECOVER with rollback → PASSED/FAILED. Emits JSONL trace events, writes atomic task.json, and returns a RunSummary.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest class in engine.py (~207 lines); tracks current_state, failed_step_id, error_code, and step_attempts.

nodes.name: Step
nodes.summary: Immutable step record with id, operation, MappingProxyType arguments/verifier, timeout_seconds, max_retries, and optional rollback. Validates types against OP_ARG_SCHEMAS at construction.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclass wrapped in MappingProxyType; construction is the single validation chokepoint.

nodes.name: Scenario
nodes.summary: Top-level immutable scenario container: version, task_id, session_id, pid, display, CellView, and ordered tuple of Steps. Validates the whole tree, rejects duplicate step IDs and unknown fields, and round-trips through to_dict/from_dict.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest class in model.py; raises ScenarioValidationError(path=...) on any rule violation; CellView is a small companion frozen dataclass.

nodes.name: _DisplayLock
nodes.summary: Per-DISPLAY exclusive flock under ~/.cache/virtuoso_bridge/x11-locks/. Acquired with LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB; raises LockHeldError if another run holds it; records the holder's PID in the lock file.
nodes.languageNotes: Context-manager protocol (`__enter__`/`__exit__`); one lock per DISPLAY string, sanitized via regex.

nodes.name: LiveExecutor
nodes.summary: Real vcli/X11 executor (898 lines, ~25 methods). Implements all five phases by translating DSL operations into fixed `vcli` argv calls through the injected command runner. Manages session binding, lock lifecycle, direct vs helper path, action-x11 batching, and typed-input sanitization in all error paths.
nodes.languageNotes: Heaviest module in the package; uses MappingProxyType for argv construction, regex for argv templating, fcntl for the display lock, and structured error dicts throughout.

nodes.name: LocalExecutor
nodes.summary: xdotool-based executor for local DISPLAY targets. Binds the window by PID at precheck, dispatches click/type/key/scroll/screenshot directly via xdotool and ImageMagick import, supports geometry-aware relative→absolute coord conversion, and rejects VCLI_LOAD/VCLI_CALL (use LiveExecutor for those).
nodes.languageNotes: ~406 lines, ~14 methods; uses subprocess.run through a private _run wrapper; private helpers _xdotool, _window_geometry, _absolute_coords, _screenshot.

nodes.name: Trace
nodes.summary: Append-only JSONL writer that opens lazily, flushes after every emit(), increments a monotonic seq counter, and stamps each Event with UTC ISO-8601 ts.
nodes.languageNotes: Lazy file open in _open(); explicit close() resets _file so a Trace can be reused.

nodes.name: TestLocalRunner
nodes.summary: Covers LocalRunner: argv-list form, env cleaning, VCLI_CAPABILITY=admin, timeout → timed_out, non-zero exit reporting, string-argv rejection, empty-argv rejection, and argv-element NUL/newline rejection.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses sys.executable as the test binary so the suite runs on any host; tolerates macOS __CF_* / LC_CTYPE leak.

nodes.name: TestSshRunnerValidation
nodes.summary: Covers SshRunner argv safety: host regex enforcement, vcli-path requirement, NUL/newline rejection, shlex.quote correctness, and rejection of any argv element that isn't the configured vcli binary.
nodes.languageNotes: 10 test methods; focused entirely on construction-time rejection paths.

nodes.name: TestFakeExecutorPerPhase
nodes.summary: Validates FakeExecutor behavior across all five phases: default SUCCESS, per-attempt outcomes, execute failure at attempt 0 / success at attempt 1, verify and recover failure paths.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses outcomes_to_dict helper to build the (step, phase, attempt) → outcome map.

nodes.name: TestRunnerHappyPath
nodes.summary: Happy-path Runner tests: both steps pass → RunSummary(passed=True), atomic task.json contains expected summary fields, output directory is created, trace has correct event sequence.
nodes.languageNotes: Warnings.simplefilter('error') to catch any DeprecationWarning leaked from the Runner.

nodes.name: TestExecuteFailRecoverSuccess
nodes.summary: Verifies that when execute fails, recover is invoked and the step can move on, producing a passing summary and a recover trace event.
nodes.languageNotes: Two test methods covering recover-success and recover-failure-then-final-failed.

nodes.name: TestPrecheck
nodes.summary: Largest test class (145 lines, 13 methods) covering LiveExecutor.precheck: missing session, port mismatch, PID zero / fallback, DISPLAY mismatch, zero/multiple windows, lock conflict, and the pid-fallback path.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds scripted FakeRunner responses that mimic real vcli JSON for sessions list, windows list, and dismiss-dialog.

nodes.name: TestExecuteMapping
nodes.summary: Maps every supported DSL operation (WINDOW_ACTIVATE, KEY, TYPE, CLICK_REL/ABS, DOUBLE_CLICK, DRAG_REL, SCROLL, MINIMIZE, MAXIMIZE, CLOSE, DISMISS_DIALOG) onto the exact `vcli window action-x11` argv the live executor must produce.
nodes.languageNotes: 10 test methods; asserts exact argv lists against expected_vcli_argv snapshots.

nodes.name: TestRecover
nodes.summary: Covers recover-phase dispatch: every rollback shape maps to a fixed vcli argv, only validated rollback operations are accepted, and rollback failure is reported with a structured error.
nodes.languageNotes: 4 test methods; cross-checks LiveExecutor.recover output against expected argv + RunSummary.

nodes.name: TestNewOperationsLive
nodes.summary: Live-executor coverage for newer DSL operations (drag-rel sequence, scroll, window-id disambiguation, session-aware argv). Confirms vcli receives the exact argv the design specifies.
nodes.languageNotes: 8 methods; uses scripted FakeRunner to capture argv and inspect argv content.

nodes.name: TestWindowIdDisambiguation
nodes.summary: Ensures LiveExecutor picks the correct window when multiple are returned (title/class/geometry filters) and forwards --window-id to every vcli call.
nodes.languageNotes: 3 methods; constructs multi-window WINDOWS_* fixtures with different pid/title/geometry.

nodes.name: TestNewVerifierPredicatesLive
nodes.summary: Live-executor verifier coverage for state_matches, title_matches, geometry_matches, ciw_eval — every predicate routes to a specific vcli query and returns the expected bool.
nodes.languageNotes: 5 methods; depends on scripted vcli responses for ciw_eval and geometry.

nodes.name: TestDynamicCiwCoordinates
nodes.summary: Covers dynamic CIW coordinate fetching at execute time: LiveExecutor queries window geometry via vcli, converts relative CLICK_REL coords to absolute, and forwards them to action-x11.
nodes.languageNotes: 4 methods; uses scripted geometry responses to drive the conversion.

nodes.name: TestLocalExecutorPrecheck
nodes.summary: LocalExecutor precheck tests: xdotool missing, DISPLAY unreachable, no-window-for-pid, window-found, explicit --window-id override skipping discovery.
nodes.languageNotes: 6 methods; heavily uses @mock.patch on shutil.which and _run.

nodes.name: TestLocalExecutorExecute
nodes.summary: LocalExecutor execute coverage: every supported operation maps to the correct xdotool command (windowactivate, key, type, click, double-click, drag, scroll, minimize/maximize, screenshot, dismiss-dialog, close). VCLI_LOAD and VCLI_CALL are rejected as fail-closed.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest class in test_local_executor (96 lines, 11 methods); asserts exact xdotool argv.

nodes.name: TestLocalExecutorVerify
nodes.summary: LocalExecutor verify-predicate tests: window_exists, state_matches, title_matches, geometry_matches; each routes through xdotool search/getactivewindow/getwindowname/getwindowgeometry.
nodes.languageNotes: 5 methods; mocks subprocess.run for every xdotool subcommand.

nodes.name: TestLocalExecutorRecover
nodes.summary: LocalExecutor recover coverage: every rollback shape (close, activate, key, type) runs the correct xdotool command; unsupported rollbacks fail closed with a structured error.
nodes.languageNotes: 5 methods; uses mocked xdotool responses and asserts recovered state.

nodes.name: TestLocalExecutorGeometryGuard
nodes.summary: Guards against GeometryError when the bound window disappears mid-run (e.g. xdotool search returns empty, geometry query fails). Verifies local executor reports the error and stops cleanly.
nodes.languageNotes: 7 methods; uses side_effect lists to drive multiple subprocess.run calls per test.

nodes.name: TestOperationArgumentTypes
nodes.summary: Largest test class in test_model (140 lines, 20 methods): exhaustive per-operation argument-type validation — strict int (no bool), positive integer bounds, allowed state strings, allowed scroll directions, allowed predicate names, optional vs required keys, and rejection of unknown keys.

nodes.name: TestVerifierValidation
nodes.summary: Covers every supported verifier predicate (window_exists, state_matches, title_matches, geometry_matches, ciw_eval): required keys, expected-type matching, and rejection of unknown predicates at parse time.
nodes.languageNotes: 10 methods; uses a parametrized helper to assert error paths.

nodes.name: TestRollbackValidation
nodes.summary: Validates rollback shapes: only already-validated operations are accepted, required keys are enforced, and unsupported rollback ops fail at parse time.
nodes.languageNotes: 8 methods; cross-checks accepted/rejected rollback ops against the model allowlist.

nodes.name: TestDeepImmutability
nodes.summary: Asserts that Scenario / Step / CellView / arguments / verifier are all deeply frozen (MappingProxyType, tuple, frozenset) — mutations at any level raise TypeError.
nodes.languageNotes: 6 methods; probes attributes, mapping methods, and nested dict values.

nodes.name: TestNewOperations

nodes.name: TestOperationArguments
nodes.summary: Confirms OP_ARG_SCHEMAS enforcement: required keys must be present, unknown keys are rejected, and the optional/required split is honored for each operation.
nodes.languageNotes: 4 methods; uses per-operation dicts to construct minimal valid steps.

nodes.name: TestNewVerifierPredicates

nodes.languageNotes: 5 methods; small focused validator tests.

nodes.name: gui_runner.py

nodes.name: test_command_runner.py

nodes.name: test_engine.py

nodes.languageNotes: unittest TestCase classes; tempfile + monkeypatched os.replace for atomic write tests.

nodes.name: test_live_executor.py

Covers construction, precheck (session/port/PID/DISPLAY/window-id/lock), baseline sanitization, DSL→vcli argv mapping, verify predicate flow, recover rollback allowlist, typed-text sanitization, lock lifecycle, new operations (SCROLL etc.), new verifier predicates, window-id disambiguation, session-aware argv, and dynamic CIW coordinates. No real ssh/vcli/X11 invoked — all I/O goes through an injected FakeRunner.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of unittest.mock; builds FakeRunner that records call args; parameterized scenarios via dict literals.

nodes.name: test_local_executor.py

Covers precheck (xdotool missing / DISPLAY unreachable / no window / window found), baseline screenshot, execute mapping for every DSL operation including SCROLL, verify predicates, recover rollback, and geometry/identity guards. subprocess.run is mocked throughout.
nodes.languageNotes: unittest.mock.patch on subprocess.run; MappingProxyType arguments for step fixtures.

nodes.name: test_model.py
nodes.summary: Extensive unittest suite for model. Covers Operation enum membership, CellView formatting, version/task_id rules, timeout/retry bounds, per-operation argument required/optional/type validation, strict-int (bool rejected), JSON deep immutability, non-JSON rejection, verifier predicate allowlist, window_wait state allowlist, rollback validation, and round-trip serialization.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-Python unit tests; uses MappingProxyType to assert deep immutability; comprehensive parameterized TestCase classes.

nodes.name: command_runner.py
nodes.summary: Hardened subprocess transport for vcli. Provides CommandError/CommandResult dataclasses plus CommandRunner base, LocalRunner (shell=False, cleaned env), and SshRunner (fixed vcli argv only; argv[0] must be the configured vcli path; NUL/newline rejected; shell-quoted remote command).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses subprocess.run with shell=False; regex allowlist for SSH host; env allowlist keeps PATH/LANG/HOME/XDG_CACHE_HOME/VB_PORT/VB_REMOTE_HOST plus VCLI_CAPABILITY=admin.

nodes.name: engine.py
nodes.summary: Scenario state machine and abstract Executor protocol. Defines RunState/StepPhase/StepOutcome enums, FakeExecutor (deterministic per-(step,phase,attempt) outcomes), and Runner that drives precheck → baseline → execute → verify → recover with bounded retries and appends atomic task.json + JSONL trace.
nodes.languageNotes: Abstract base Executor with precheck/baseline/execute/verify/recover hooks; dataclass RunSummary; Runner emits trace events and writes task.json atomically.

nodes.name: live_executor.py
nodes.summary: Real vcli/SSH executor implementing the Executor protocol. Precheck binds session/PID/DISPLAY/window-id; per-run flock serializes DISPLAY access; every GUI action routes through vcli window action-x11; typed input text is sanitized out of errors and argv logs.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy module (~1k LOC); uses fcntl.flock, pathlib, errno, uuid; maps DSL operations to fixed vcli argv; supports --direct and action-x11-batch fast paths.

nodes.name: local_executor.py
nodes.summary: Direct xdotool Executor for local X11. No vcli indirection; binds the target window by PID; supports SCROLL via xdotool buttons 4/5/6/7; fails closed on geometry/identity mismatches.
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps subprocess.run against xdotool key/type/click/drag/scroll; mocks cleanly via subprocess for tests.

nodes.name: model.py
nodes.summary: Strict scenario DSL parser. Defines the Operation enum and per-operation required/optional argument schemas, integer/button/string/list/dict arg classifications, verifier predicate allowlist, deeply immutable dataclasses (CellView/Step/Scenario), and ScenarioValidationError raised with a JSON-pointer-style path.
nodes.languageNotes: dataclass(frozen=True) plus MappingProxyType/tuple freezing for deep immutability; reject-closed validation against explicit allowlists.

nodes.name: trace.py
nodes.summary: Append-only JSONL event log with immediate flush per emit. Event dataclass carries seq/timestamp/state/step/attempt/outcome/duration/details; Trace opens lazily and flushes after every line so logs survive crashes.
nodes.languageNotes: Lightweight; uses dataclasses.asdict and datetime timezone-aware isoformat.

nodes.summary: Loads a scenario, builds the executor, runs it through the Runner, then emits a final JSON line and returns the exit code.

nodes.name: daemon.rs
nodes.summary: Synchronous `NativeTransportClient` (Unix-only) that talks the versioned IPC protocol to the transport daemon. Implements `RemoteTransport` over a length-prefixed JSON frame channel on a Unix domain socket: performs the `Hello` handshake (profile, auth token, daemon nonce), then offers test_connection / run_command / upload_file|upload_text / download_file|download_dir / challenge / request_shutdown. Also owns the end-to-end integration `mod tests` that round-trips through the real server.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust, edition per workspace Cargo.toml. Module gated on `(unix, any(test, feature = "native-ssh"))` where applicable; serde for JSON wire types; std-only framing layer (no tokio, no russh at the IPC layer).

nodes.name: framing.rs
nodes.summary: Transport-agnostic byte framing for the IPC protocol: four-byte big-endian length prefix + UTF-8 payload, with an 8 MiB hard ceiling (`MAX_FRAME_SIZE`). Exposes `encode_frame`, `FrameReader<R: Read>` (streaming, deadline-aware `read_frame_until`/`read_frame_until_with`), and `FrameWriter<W: Write>` (`write_frame_with_deadline`). `FrameError` covers TooLarge, Truncated, and Io variants. The layer never sees SSH, Tokio, or daemon-internal types.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust, edition per workspace Cargo.toml. Module gated on `(unix, any(test, feature = "native-ssh"))` where applicable; serde for JSON wire types; std-only framing layer (no tokio, no russh at the IPC layer).

nodes.name: messages.rs
nodes.summary: Plain `serde` request/response vocabulary for the IPC protocol: `ProtocolVersion` (major/minor, current constants pulled from `framing`, major must match exactly), `Operation` enum (Hello, RunCommand, UploadFile, DownloadDir, Health, Shutdown, etc., with custom serde via `as_str`), `Hello`/`HelloAck`, `RequestEnvelope`/`ResponseEnvelope`/`ResponseResult`, and the `IpcError` taxonomy (codes, connection-level predicate, and From impls for serde_json / std::io errors).
nodes.languageNotes: Rust, edition per workspace Cargo.toml. Module gated on `(unix, any(test, feature = "native-ssh"))` where applicable; serde for JSON wire types; std-only framing layer (no tokio, no russh at the IPC layer).

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for `transport::ipc`. Declares `daemon`, `framing`, `messages`, and `server` submodules, with `daemon`/`server` gated on `(unix, any(test, feature = "native-ssh"))` because the real daemon is feature-gated but the test suite exercises the same code. The module owns only the wire format; no russh, Tokio, SSH, or daemon-internal types leak.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust, edition per workspace Cargo.toml. Module gated on `(unix, any(test, feature = "native-ssh"))` where applicable; serde for JSON wire types; std-only framing layer (no tokio, no russh at the IPC layer).

nodes.name: server.rs
nodes.summary: Server half of the versioned IPC protocol (Unix-only). `serve_one` / `serve_one_with_shutdown` handle a single connection: `Hello` handshake, then dispatch every subsequent `RequestEnvelope` onto the supplied `RemoteTransport` (or an `EndpointPool` via `serve_one_pooled`/`run_with_pool`) until the peer closes. `dispatch` is the central request router (~130 lines, handles RunCommand, uploads, downloads, Health, Shutdown, Challenge, Cancel, local-forward). `run` binds the Unix socket, sets mode `0600`, and accepts forever. Implements the Tier-1 liveness `Challenge` probe by answering with the recorded daemon nonce.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust, edition per workspace Cargo.toml. Module gated on `(unix, any(test, feature = "native-ssh"))` where applicable; serde for JSON wire types; std-only framing layer (no tokio, no russh at the IPC layer).

nodes.name: skill_db.py
nodes.summary: SQLite-backed persistent knowledge store for the Virtuoso SKILL API (virtuoso-gui-debug skill). Defines DB_PATH and exposes connection management plus CRUD helpers: get_db (lazy schema creation for functions, error_history, layers, shapes, fnd_functions, param_examples tables), record_function, record_failure, has_known_failure, get_known_functions, get_function, record_layer, record_shape_property, record_param_example, get_param_examples, and stats. Each writer stamps an ISO timestamp and commits; readers project sqlite3.Row rows into dicts. Forms the persistence layer every other script in this skill imports.
nodes.languageNotes: Python 3 with stdlib sqlite3 only; uses Path for filesystem layout, dict-row projection via sqlite3.Row. No third-party deps. ~215 lines, 11 functions, no classes.

nodes.name: get_db
nodes.summary: Opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at DB_PATH and ensures the full schema (functions, error_history, layers, shapes, fnd_functions, param_examples) exists via idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements. Returns a connection with row_factory=sqlite3.Row.
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 19-66; calls sqlite3.connect, conn.execute (x4), conn.commit.

nodes.name: record_function
nodes.summary: Inserts or updates a row in the functions table for a discovered SKILL function, splitting the dotted name into category prefix and writing existence flag, signature, description, notes, and a current ISO timestamp.
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 69-85; ~17 lines, single INSERT OR REPLACE.

nodes.name: record_failure
nodes.summary: Logs a probe failure into error_history with error_type, error_message, and an ISO timestamp, used to track which functions are known broken so future runs skip them.
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 88-94; single INSERT.

nodes.name: has_known_failure
nodes.summary: Returns the most recent unresolved error_history row for a given function_name (fixed=0) or None if there is no open failure. Used to short-circuit re-probing of broken functions.
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 97-104; SELECT with LIMIT 1, dict projection.

nodes.name: get_known_functions
nodes.summary: Lists known-working SKILL functions. Overload: with a category argument returns rows for that category only; without it returns all func_exists=1 rows ordered by category, name. Each row is projected to a dict.
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 107-116; two SELECT branches based on whether category is provided.

nodes.name: record_param_example
nodes.summary: Records a working example value for a parameter of a SKILL function, incrementing its success_count via a conditional UPDATE (or inserting a new row) so frequently-successful examples bubble to the top of get_param_examples results.
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 149-168; ~20 lines combining UPDATE-then-INSERT and a trailing commit.

nodes.name: stats
nodes.summary: Aggregates row counts across all tables (functions, functions where func_exists=1, drawable layers, working shapes, fnd_functions, unresolved error_history) and formats them as a multi-line summary string with str() casts.
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 191-207; six COUNT(*) SELECTs and string assembly.

nodes.name: enumerate_functions.py
nodes.summary: Discovers SKILL functions by name pattern for the virtuoso-gui-debug skill. Generates candidate names from prefix x entity combinations (build_candidates), probes each candidate by invoking `name()` via vcli skill exec (test_function, classifies 'undefined' vs arg-count error responses), and orchestrates a filtered run with optional --session and --prefix CLI args (run_enumeration). Every successful probe is recorded through skill_db.record_function, while known-broken functions are skipped via has_known_failure.
nodes.languageNotes: Python 3 script using subprocess.run to shell out to vcli, json.loads to parse responses, and argparse for CLI. Imports get_db/record_function/record_layer/record_shape_property from sibling skill_db. ~157 lines, 3 functions, no classes.

nodes.name: test_function
nodes.summary: Calls a single SKILL function name via vcli skill exec with no args, parses the JSON envelope, classifies the response (undefined function vs arg-count error vs generic failure), and lower-cases a combined stdout+stderr snippet for downstream matching. Returns a JSON-friendly result tuple/dict.
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 62-109; ~48 lines, subprocess + JSON parsing, multiple decision branches.

nodes.name: run_enumeration
nodes.summary: Driver that opens the DB, builds the candidate list (optionally filtered by prefix), iterates with progress reporting, calls test_function for each candidate, and persists results through record_function. Prints progress counts at intervals and a final summary.
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 112-143; ~32 lines, the entrypoint function for the script.

nodes.name: probe_signatures.py
nodes.summary: Reverse-engineers SKILL function argument counts by invoking each known function with 0..5 nil arguments and parsing the error message to recover the expected arity and a cleaned signature string. Wraps a per-function probe (probe_signature) and a batch driver (run_signature_probe) that reads the candidate list from skill_db.get_known_functions, threads Popen subprocess calls with a short timeout, and stores results back via skill_db.record_function.
nodes.languageNotes: Python 3 using subprocess.Popen + communicate, re.search for arity regex, and sqlite3 rows via skill_db. ~94 lines, 2 functions, no classes.

nodes.name: probe_signature
nodes.summary: Calls a single SKILL function with 0..5 nil arguments via vcli, collects the resulting error messages, regex-extracts the expected argument count, and returns (arg_count, signature) or (None, None) when no signal is recoverable.
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 16-57; ~42 lines, Popen + communicate + re.search + int coercion.

nodes.name: run_signature_probe
nodes.summary: Batch driver: loads candidate functions from skill_db (filtered by --limit), calls probe_signature on each, aggregates results into a per-category signature summary, and persists updated records back through record_function. Prints per-stage progress and totals.
nodes.languageNotes: Lines 60-87; ~28 lines, the script's entrypoint.

nodes.name: skill_db.py
nodes.summary: SQLite-backed persistent knowledge store for the virtuoso-gui-debug skill. Owns the schema (functions, layers, shapes, error_history, param_examples, fnd_functions) and exposes a set of record/query helpers that other debug scripts use to remember which SKILL functions exist, what their signatures look like, which layers are drawable, which shape properties work, and which parameter values have been validated.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure standard library (sqlite3, json, os, datetime, pathlib). Uses sqlite3.Row for dict-like rows. All writers use UPSERT (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) and bump test_count / success_count so each call strengthens the stored knowledge.

nodes.name: enumerate_functions.py
nodes.summary: Generator/prober that discovers which Cadence SKILL functions exist in a running Virtuoso session. Builds a candidate name list from PREFIXES x ENTITIES plus a STANDALONE list, invokes each via `vcli skill exec <name>()`, parses the JSON status, distinguishes 'undefined function' from real arg errors, and persists results through skill_db.
nodes.languageNotes: Drives `vcli` via subprocess.run with a 15s timeout. sys.path is extended at import time so the sibling skill_db.py can be imported directly. Distinguishes 'undefined' vs 'wrong args' by scanning both the JSON `output` and `errors` fields.

nodes.name: probe_signatures.py
nodes.summary: Second-pass signature extractor: for functions already known to exist (from enumerate_functions), it calls each one with 0..5 nil arguments via vcli, harvests the error messages, and uses a regex on `N expected, M given` to infer arity. The aggregated probe results are then written back as a compact signature string per function.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses subprocess.Popen + communicate(timeout=10) per probe so a slow SKILL call cannot stall the loop. Failure-tolerant by design: any single bad probe is skipped and the function keeps going.

nodes.name: get_db
nodes.summary: Opens the SQLite database at <skill>/data/skill_db.sqlite3 with row_factory=sqlite3.Row and idempotently creates the functions, layers, shapes, and error_history tables. Returns the live connection; every other module in this skill calls this first.
nodes.languageNotes: Single CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS per table, single commit. Path is resolved relative to the module's parent.parent (skill root).

nodes.name: record_function
nodes.summary: Upserts a function row with category derived from the leading underscore-delimited token, bumps test_count, and refreshes last_tested / signature / description / notes on conflict.
nodes.languageNotes: Category heuristic: name.split('_')[0] if '_' in name else name[:8]. COALESCE in the ON CONFLICT clause preserves prior values when new ones are None.

nodes.name: record_failure
nodes.summary: Inserts a row into error_history with fixed=0 so the recurring-self-improvement loop can avoid re-trying the same broken call. Truncates error_message to 500 chars.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain INSERT, no upsert. Timestamps via datetime.now().isoformat() stored alongside the SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP default.

nodes.name: has_known_failure
nodes.summary: Looks up the most recent unresolved (fixed=0) error row for a function. Returns a dict with error_type/error_message/created_at, or None if the function has no open failures.
nodes.languageNotes: ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1 — most recent only.

nodes.name: get_known_functions
nodes.summary: Returns all functions where func_exists=1, optionally filtered by category. Used by probe_signatures as the worklist for the second pass.
nodes.languageNotes: Two SQL branches: one with WHERE category=?, one without, both ordered (by name when filtered, by category,name otherwise).

nodes.name: get_function
nodes.summary: Single-row lookup by primary key; returns a dict via sqlite3.Row or None.
nodes.languageNotes: Two lines — SELECT ... WHERE name=? then dict(row) or None.

nodes.name: record_layer
nodes.summary: Upserts a (layer, purpose) row marking whether the layer/purpose combination is drawable.
nodes.languageNotes: Composite primary key (layer, purpose); ON CONFLICT updates drawable + last_tested only.

nodes.name: record_shape_property
nodes.summary: Upserts a (obj_type, property_name) row recording whether the property works and an example value. COALESCE preserves the existing example when the new one is None.
nodes.languageNotes: Composite primary key (obj_type, property_name); works coerced via int() to 0/1.

nodes.name: record_param_example
nodes.summary: Creates the param_examples table on first use and upserts a (function, param, value) row, incrementing success_count and refreshing last_used on conflict.
nodes.languageNotes: Lazy CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, then ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE that only touches success_count and last_used. Identical CREATE is repeated in get_param_examples — slight redundancy.

nodes.name: get_param_examples
nodes.summary: Returns known-good parameter values for a function, ordered by success_count DESC. Same lazy CREATE as record_param_example ensures the table exists on first read.
nodes.languageNotes: SELECT param_name, example_value, success_count ... ORDER BY success_count DESC. Duplicates the CREATE TABLE statement from record_param_example.

nodes.name: stats
nodes.summary: Aggregates counts across all tables (functions, drawable layers, verified shape properties, fnd_functions, open errors) plus the DB path. Used as a self-test / dashboard print at the bottom of the script.
nodes.languageNotes: Six scalar SELECT COUNT(*) queries; the fnd_functions SELECT will raise if that table was never created (no IF NOT EXISTS here).

nodes.name: build_candidates
nodes.summary: Generates the full sorted set of candidate SKILL function names by taking the cartesian product of the PREFIXES x ENTITIES lists plus the STANDALONE list, then dedupes via set() and sorts.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-Python: nested for loops + set + sorted. No I/O.

nodes.name: test_function
nodes.summary: Calls `vcli skill exec <name>()` and classifies the response: empty output -> does not exist; status=success -> exists with no signature; status=error -> exists with arity-error signature; 'undefined function' substring -> does not exist. Handles subprocess.TimeoutExpired and arbitrary exceptions.
nodes.languageNotes: 15s subprocess timeout. Reads BOTH output and errors fields of the vcli JSON envelope, then lower-cases the joined text before substring matching.

nodes.name: run_enumeration
nodes.summary: Orchestrator: opens the DB, builds (optionally prefix-filtered) candidates, loops and records each as exists/missing/timeout/exception via skill_db.record_function, and prints a progress summary.
nodes.languageNotes: Tri-state exists/missing from test_function. Imports record_layer and record_shape_property from skill_db even though they are not used here — keeps the surface area aligned with future probes.

nodes.name: probe_signature
nodes.summary: For a single SKILL function name, invokes it with 0..5 nil arguments, parses each response, and on 'error' status tries to extract the expected-arity from 'N expected, M given' via regex. Returns a dict {nargs: message}.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses subprocess.Popen + communicate(timeout=10). Any per-call exception is caught and the loop continues, so one slow probe cannot block the whole batch.

nodes.name: run_signature_probe
nodes.summary: Reads known functions from skill_db (optionally truncated by --limit), probes each via probe_signature, concatenates per-nargs messages into a ' | '-joined signature string, and persists it via record_function.
nodes.languageNotes: Prints a progress line every 20 probes. CLI entry point at module bottom reads vcli path from ~/.local/bin and the session id from sys.argv.

nodes.name: ci.yml (CI workflow)
nodes.summary: Primary CI workflow for the Rust workspace. Triggers on push and PR to main. Runs four jobs sequentially-on-same-runner (each independent runner, no needs): (1) check — fmt --check + clippy with -D warnings across default, --features daemon, and --features native-ssh; (2) test — cargo test on default features; (3) build — cargo build for default and --features daemon; (4) audit — pinned cargo-audit 0.22.2 with --ignore RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin RSA timing side-channel, reachable only via ssh-key->russh under native-ssh; full rationale in audit.toml). Uses actions/checkout@v7, dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable (with clippy, rustfmt for check), and Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 on every job. CARGO_TERM_COLOR=always. 59 lines / 4 jobs.
nodes.languageNotes: YAML workflow with 4 top-level keys (name, on, env, jobs) and 4 job definitions. Steps use both `uses:` (third-party actions) and `run:` (shell). Inline `#` comment block in audit step explains the RUSTSEC ignore.

nodes.name: integration.yml (Integration Matrix)
nodes.summary: Cross-platform feature matrix workflow, labeled as 'Step 7 of the native-transport plan'. Triggers on push and PR to main. One matrix job (`matrix`) with fail-fast: false spanning os={ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest} x features={default, native-ssh} — six cells total, each builds and tests with `cargo build` and `cargo test`, conditionally adding `--features native-ssh` when matrix.features != 'default' (YAML `format()` expression). The header comment explicitly states the goal: catch Windows-only native build breaks here rather than at release time, and avoid one OS masking another via fail-fast:false. 34 lines / 1 matrix job / 6 effective jobs.
nodes.languageNotes: YAML workflow with 4 top-level keys plus a 5-line header comment block explaining the native-transport plan context. Uses GitHub Actions ${{ matrix.* }} and format() expressions to conditionally inject --features. 6 cells = 3 OS x 2 features.

nodes.name: release.yml (Release workflow)
nodes.summary: Tag-driven release workflow that builds, packages, and uploads binaries plus optionally publishes to crates.io. Triggers on push of v* tags. Five jobs with explicit needs: (1) build-linux-x86_64 — ubuntu-latest, builds vcli/vtui with --features native-ssh and virtuoso-daemon with --features daemon, packages as `dist/{vcli,vtui,virtuoso-daemon}-${TAG}-linux-x86_64`, uploads via softprops/action-gh-release@v3 with auto-generated notes pointing to CHANGELOG.md; (2) build-linux-aarch64 — ubuntu-latest with aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu target, installs gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu, patches ~/.cargo/config.toml with the linker, daemon-only build, uploads daemon only; (3) build-macos-aarch64 — macos-latest (Apple Silicon), same triple-binary packaging; (4) build-windows-x86_64 — windows-latest with shell:bash for packaging, .exe suffix; (5) publish-crate — gated on all four builds, uses CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN secret, idempotent (skips silently if token unset or version already published). permissions: contents: write. 159 lines / 5 jobs.
nodes.languageNotes: YAML workflow with 5 top-level keys (name, on, env, permissions, jobs). nodes.name: Recreate a Schematic from an Existing Design
nodes.summary: Workflow for reading an existing schematic, mapping instances to a uniform grid, and redrawing cleanly with net stubs. Three steps: (1) read original via `virtuoso_bridge.virtuoso.schematic.reader.read_schematic(client, LIB, CELL, include_positions=True)`, (2) map to grid — sort by y for rows, sort by x within row for columns, identify differential pairs (R0 left / MY mirrored right), choose GRID spacing (1.5 recommended), (3) redraw using `client.schematic.edit()` with placement tuples `(name, cell, col, row, orient)` and connectivity labels `(name, drain, gate, source, body)` using `add_net_label_to_transistor`. Key rules: GRID=1.5, NMOS at bottom rows / PMOS at top, pins in dedicated leftmost column (col=-1), output stages offset right (col 5-6), no explicit wires (only labels, same net name = same net), verify with CIW screenshot after every run.

nodes.name: gui_click.sh
nodes.summary: Shell script that performs a mouse click at absolute screen coordinates via xdotool, with optional mouse-button and click-count selection. Activates the previously locked window (state from gui_find.sh), moves the cursor, clicks, then auto-captures a verify screenshot via ImageMagick `import` and writes a structured line to /tmp/gui_actions.log.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with `set -u`. Pairs arguments with manual while/case flag parser (no getopts). Sources /tmp/gui_session.env to read GUI_WID produced by gui_find.sh. Logs only token-level data to /tmp/gui_actions.log (window id, button, count, shot path) — coordinates but no content secrets.

nodes.name: gui_drag.sh
nodes.summary: Shell script that executes a smooth mouse drag between two absolute screen points by interpolating intermediate positions with xdotool mousedown / mousemove / mouseup. Configurable button (left/middle/right) and step count (default 8) for trajectory smoothness. Logs the drag to /tmp/gui_actions.log.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with `set -u`. Uses integer arithmetic (`$(( X1 + (X2 - X1) * i / STEPS ))`) and a `for` loop driven by `seq 1 $STEPS` for step interpolation. Sources /tmp/gui_session.env for the locked window id. 42 lines — one of the longer scripts in the toolkit.

nodes.name: gui_env.sh
nodes.summary: Shell preflight check that verifies the X11 GUI-driver prerequisites: DISPLAY is set, session is not Wayland (xdotool requires X), and the `xdotool` binary exists. Issues a non-fatal warning if neither `import` (ImageMagick) nor `scrot` is installed for the screenshot channel. Reports display geometry via `xdotool getdisplaygeometry`.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with `set -u`. Pure precondition gate: each unmet check exits with a numbered ERROR or a single WARN. Used by smoke.sh as the first smoke-test stage and is the canonical entry point for diagnosing missing-tool errors.

nodes.name: gui_find.sh
nodes.summary: Shell script that searches for a visible X11 window by name then class via xdotool, takes the first match, and persists its window id as `GUI_WID` into the shared state file (default /tmp/gui_session.env). All later click/type actions in this session are then window-scoped to that id. Logs the lock event to /tmp/gui_actions.log.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with `set -u`. This is the only script that WRITES the session state file (using `export GUI_WID=…`); the other scripts source it read-only. Two-pass search (`--name` then `--class`) makes it forgiving of regex metacharacters in arguments.

nodes.name: gui_scroll.sh
nodes.summary: Shell script that issues mouse-wheel scroll input at absolute screen coordinates. Maps the symbolic direction `up/down/left/right` onto the corresponding xdotool button codes (4/5/6/7) and emits N repeats with a small delay between clicks. Logs the scroll event to /tmp/gui_actions.log.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with `set -u`. Uses a `case` block to translate direction words into numeric xdotool button constants. Note that it does NOT source the session state file — `GUI_WID` is only referenced for logging, not for action scoping, so scroll always targets the root window.

nodes.name: gui_shot.sh
nodes.summary: Shell utility that captures the root-window screenshot to a path (default /tmp/gui_shot.png). Prefers ImageMagick `import` (matches xdotool-based workflows) and falls back to `scrot`. Exits non-zero if neither tool is present. Logs the capture to /tmp/gui_actions.log.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with `set -e` (the only script in the set that enables errexit instead of nounset). Compact `if/elif/else` over `command -v` for tool preference, then a single-shot capture. Used both stand-alone and as stage 4 of smoke.sh.

nodes.name: gui_state.sh
nodes.summary: Shell introspection helper that lists the first ~40 visible X11 windows (id / truncated name / parsed geometry) and prints the currently active window. Designed to be called during the observation phase of an OODA-style loop so the decision layer can see what is actually on screen.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with `set -u`. `for` loop over a multi-line `xdotool search` capture, per-iteration `xdotool getwindowname` + `getwindowgeometry` (parsed with awk to strip screen-offset suffix). Names are truncated to 60 chars with `head -c` to keep output compact.

nodes.name: gui_type.sh
nodes.summary: Shell script that focuses the locked window and types a text string via `xdotool type --clearmodifiers --delay …`. Default per-key delay of 30 ms to avoid dropped characters in the target application. Logs the LENGTH only to /tmp/gui_actions.log so passwords and secrets never reach the audit log.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with `set -u`. Uses `${#TEXT}` (parameter length expansion) and the `--` argument terminator on xdotool type to safely pass strings that begin with `-`. Slight enhancement over gui_click.sh: also tries `xdotool windowfocus` as a fallback before issuing keystrokes.

nodes.name: gui_wait.sh
nodes.summary: Shell polling helper that waits until a window matching a name/class substring becomes visible (`appear` mode, default) or disappears (`disappear` mode). Implements a busy-wait loop with a hard wall-clock timeout (in seconds). Exits 0 when the condition is met, 1 on timeout.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with `set -u`. Classic `deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + TIMEOUT ))` style timeout pattern. Uses `xdotool search … | wc -l` rather than capturing the PID list each iteration — cheap and adequate for window-presence checks.

nodes.name: smoke.sh
nodes.summary: Shell orchestrator that runs a 6-stage self-test of the GUI-debug toolkit: env check → launch `xmessage` → find/lock the window → pre-click screenshot → convert window-relative to absolute coordinates and click the OK button → verify the window closed. Prints `SMOKE PASS` on success, `SMOKE FAIL` plus non-zero exit on failure. Skips gracefully if `xmessage` is missing.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with `set -u`. Resolves its own directory with `HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)` to invoke its sibling scripts by relative path. Reads `eval "$(xdotool getwindowgeometry --shell …)"` (xdotool's `--shell` mode emits POSIX-shell-evaluatable assignments) to perform the relative→absolute coordinate translation for the button click. The single piece of glue that turns the atomic scripts into a closed-loop diagnose tool.

Emits a JSON systemMessage with the relative + absolute plot path on success; silently exits on non-matching or unplottable inputs. nodes.name: rust_check.sh

Reads hook JSON from stdin, gates on file extension `.rs` and a $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR path prefix, then runs `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` before/after a `cargo fmt --quiet` to detect auto-fixes (emitting a systemMessage when a fix was applied). nodes.name: SKILL nil return is not a transport error

Consequence: `if !result.ok() { return Err(...) }` guards only catch daemon errors and timeouts, never SKILL-level failures. Provides a fix pattern (check `output.trim() == "nil"` as well) and a special-case rule for list commands (maeGetEnabledAnalysis, maeGetSessions, maeGetResultTests) where SKILL `nil` means 'empty list', solved by wrapping with `skill_strings_to_json()` so the layer always returns a JSON array and checking only `r.ok()` in the command layer. layers.name: Rust Binary Entrypoints
layers.description: Top-level binary entry points for the three Rust binaries: the main vcli CLI, the vtui TUI, and the feature-gated virtuoso-daemon bridge relay.

layers.description: Clap subcommand handlers under src/commands/ that expose CLI verbs (session, maestro, library, skill, symbol, design, layout, schematic, config, process, etc.) and dispatch them onto the bridge or local subsystems.

layers.name: Virtuoso Bridge Layer
layers.description: TCP bridge to a running Virtuoso process under src/client/: SKILL/IPC bridge, batch schema, and per-domain operation modules (library, layout, schematic, symbol, skill, window, ocean*, whitelist, editor).

layers.name: Transport Layer
layers.description: SSH tunnel, Unix-domain-socket IPC, host-key and identity handling, native SSH backend (russh), OpenSSH subprocess backend, pool/scheduler, daemon lifecycle, and X11 forwarding plumbing under src/transport/.

layers.name: TUI Layer
layers.description: ratatui-based terminal UI under src/tui/: event loop, app state/action/event/overlay/data submodules, theme, and per-tab render widgets (sessions, jobs, config, chrome, footer, overlays).

layers.name: Domain Modules
layers.description: EDA-domain parsers and evaluators under src/spectre/ (netlist, PSF, maestro CSV, runner, persistent job tracker) and src/ocean/ (Ocean expression evaluator and corner handling).

layers.name: Jobs & State Layer
layers.description: Background-job state, history, async runtime, session heartbeat, and command log: src/jobs/, src/history.rs, src/async_runtime.rs, src/command_log.rs, src/session/, src/streaming/, and the integration test harness files src/tests.rs + src/test_env.rs.

layers.name: Plugin & Capability Layer

layers.name: Cross-cutting Infrastructure
layers.description: Cross-cutting Rust infrastructure: error types, configuration, data models, output formatting, runtime paths, authentication, audit logging, RPC dispatch + schema, MCP server, skill discovery (SKILL), sys shims (linux_rename), and transaction diff/snapshot.

layers.name: Integration Tests

tour.title: Project Overview & Manifest
tour.description: Start at the top: README.md frames the project's three-binary split (vcli, vtui, virtuoso-daemon) and the analog-IC scope. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md lay down the contributor/agent conventions. Cargo.toml declares the workspace members, dependency policy, and feature flags that gate the daemon.
tour.languageLesson: Cargo workspace layout — three [[bin]] entries share one [lib] target so internal modules can be reused across the CLI, TUI, and daemon.

tour.title: Binary Entry Points
tour.description: Three thin main() entry points hand off to the shared library: src/main.rs is the vcli front door (arg parsing → command dispatch), src/vtui.rs boots the ratatui app, and src/daemon/main.rs is the feature-gated bridge relay that fronts a running Virtuoso instance. Reading these first shows you the contract each binary has with the rest of the codebase.
tour.languageLesson: Each main.rs is intentionally minimal (truncation and dispatch only). All reusable logic lives in src/lib.rs so the TUI and daemon can pull from the same modules as the CLI.

tour.title: CLI Subcommand Layer
tour.description: src/commands/mod.rs is the clap dispatch hub — each sibling (session, maestro, library, schematic, sim, skill, tunnel, transport_daemon, etc.) is a self-contained subcommand module that delegates into the client/ bridge. Scan this layer to learn what user-facing verbs exist before diving into how they are implemented.
tour.languageLesson: Each commands/*.rs file is a flat `pub fn handle(matches: &ArgMatches, ctx: &Context) -> Result<...>` entry point — easy to skim and to add new verbs to.

tour.title: Virtuoso Bridge (TCP/SKILL Transport Client)
tour.description: src/client/bridge.rs is the protocol client: it speaks SKILL/TCP to a running Virtuoso and dispatches requests to the specialised ops modules — maestro_ops.rs for Analog Design Environment flows, layout_ops.rs / schematic_ops.rs / library_ops.rs / window_ops.rs / editor_ops.rs for cell-level work, and skill_runtime.rs / skill_sexp.rs / whitelist.rs for sandboxed SKILL execution. Together they are the seam between the CLI and Cadence.
tour.languageLesson: Bridge ops are kept narrow on purpose — each *ops.rs is one concern (maestro vs. layout vs. library) so reviewers can find SKILL-call surface area quickly. The whitelist gates which SKILL forms are allowed to cross the trust boundary.

tour.title: Transport Layer (SSH / Native-SSH / Tunnels)
tour.description: src/transport/mod.rs is the facade over a small selection of backends — openssh.rs, native.rs (russh), ssh.rs — all sharing a common contract.rs. tunnel.rs / daemon_lifecycle.rs orchestrate port forwarding and long-lived remote sessions, while pool.rs, scheduler.rs, session_discovery.rs, host_keys.rs, auth.rs, identity.rs, and lifecycle.rs cover concurrent reuse, host-key policy, and identity file plumbing. This is how the CLI reaches a remote Cadence host.
tour.languageLesson: The `Backend` trait in contract.rs lets the CLI swap between system `ssh` (openssh.rs) and a pure-Rust russh backend (native.rs) without touching upstream call sites.

tour.title: Daemon IPC Layer
tour.description: src/transport/ipc/* is the local Unix-socket protocol used between vcli and the long-running virtuoso-daemon: messages.rs defines the wire format, framing.rs handles length-prefixed I/O, server.rs hosts incoming connections, and daemon.rs is the IPC-side bridge. This sublayer is the only way the bridge is reachable from multiple vcli processes without re-spawning SSH.
tour.languageLesson: Length-prefixed (bincode or similar) framing over a Unix-domain socket keeps the daemon IPC both fast and trivial to fuzz — see framing.rs for the codec.

tour.title: Domain Modules — Spectre & Ocean
tour.description: src/spectre/* covers the simulator side: runner.rs spawns Spectre, parsers.rs ingests raw output, jobs.rs is the persistent job tracker (with kill -0 probes and process-group cancellation), maestro_csv.rs reads ADE results, and mod.rs ties them together. src/ocean/* is the Ocean expression-language evaluator used for skill evaluation and corner sweeps. These are the simulation-domain modules the rest of the CLI plugs into.
tour.languageLesson: Job persistence is plain JSON on disk under the runtime cache — deliberately simple so that `vcli sim jobs` works without a daemon.

tour.title: TUI Layer (ratatui)
tour.description: src/tui/mod.rs boots the event loop. tui/app/{mod,state,event,action,data,overlay}.rs implement the Elm-style model (state + actions + event routing) and src/tui/ui/* draws chrome, content, jobs, sessions, config, footer and overlay widgets. theme.rs and shared.rs hold styling primitives. This is the screen a power user lives in.
tour.languageLesson: TUI follows an Elm-style architecture: events in → actions → state → frame draw — keeping side effects localised and the UI testable.

tour.title: Cross-Cutting Infrastructure
tour.description: The plumbing shared by every layer: src/error.rs is the unified error type, src/config.rs and src/config_file.rs handle layered config (defaults, files, CLI flags), src/models.rs defines the serialisable data shapes, src/output.rs controls CLI rendering (JSON, table, plain), and src/lib.rs re-exports the public API. Read these to understand how the rest of the code is glued together.
tour.languageLesson: Errors flow through a single `thiserror`-derived enum; the `Context` type threaded through every command handler carries config, paths, and runtime paths in one place.

tour.title: Plugin, Profile & Capability System
tour.description: src/capability/{mod,plugin}.rs defines the capability tokens that gate privileged SKILL calls. src/plugins/{mod,registry,schema}.rs loads third-party plugin manifests at runtime, and src/profile.rs handles named session profiles (think: named Cadence library + transport combinations). Together they let users extend the CLI without forking it.
tour.languageLesson: Capabilities are explicit allow/deny tokens attached to each SKILL call — the bridge refuses anything not on the whitelist.

tour.title: RPC, Session & Transaction Internals
tour.description: Beyond commands/, three supporting layers coordinate state: src/rpc/{mod,dispatcher,schema}.rs is the internal RPC dispatch used by the daemon, src/session/{mod,heartbeat}.rs tracks live bridge sessions and liveness probes, and src/transaction/{mod,diff,snapshot}.rs handles diffing cell/skill transactions before commit. Reading them last in the architecture section reveals how state is kept coherent across processes.
tour.languageLesson: Transactions are first-class — the diff/snapshot pair is how multi-step library edits stay consistent if the daemon dies mid-flight.

tour.title: Integration Tests
tour.description: The tests/ directory exercises the public surface end-to-end: ocean.rs and spectre.rs pin domain behaviour, skill_load.rs and skill_escape.rs gate the SKILL sandbox, maestro_csv.rs covers ADE output parsing, config.rs / config_check.rs / config_check_cli.rs verify layered config, error_handling.rs / daemon_user_guard.rs / tunnel_profile.rs / tunnel_hostname_check.rs lock down the messy bits (permission checks, SSH guardrails). These tell you what the maintainers consider sacred.
tour.languageLesson: Integration tests are kept thin and pure — they read fixtures from disk and assert on parsed/serialised output rather than spawning live tools.

tour.title: CI/CD Pipeline
tour.description: .github/workflows/* codifies the contract: ci.yml runs the rust toolchain checks, integration.yml exercises the heavier end-to-end suite, release.yml ships binaries, security-audit.yml runs cargo-audit, and skill-tests.yml validates the analog design skill catalog. Reading these tells you the policy floor: what must pass before any merge.
tour.languageLesson: Skill tests are a separate workflow — they're checked in alongside the Rust tests but use a different runner (Python fixtures).

tour.title: Analog Design Skill Catalog
tour.description: The skill catalog is the project's secret weapon: each .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md is a guided workflow for an analog IC design task. Read sim-setup for end-to-end simulation setup, maestro for ADE/maestro orchestration, and spectre-netlist-template for hand-tuned Spectre netlist patterns. Together they show how the CLI is meant to be used by an LLM agent.
tour.languageLesson: SKILL.md files follow a shared convention — frontmatter declares name/description, body is the workflow steps. Read .claude/skills/_shared/convention.md first if you plan to add one.

tour.title: CAD Knowledge Base (.pensieve/decisions)
tour.description: The .pensieve/decisions/*.md are architectural decision records — each captures a concrete 'why we did it this way' note. Read 2026-04-19-virtuoso-bridge-lite-adoption.md for the bridge topology, 2026-04-11-session-vs-profile.md for the session-vs-profile split, and 2026-05-07-async-deferred.md for the reasoning behind the synchronous-first design. These explain the trade-offs the code itself hides.
tour.languageLesson: Decision files are dated YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md and read top-down: context → options → decision → consequences. Treat them as load-bearing context before proposing major refactors.
